Package frc.robot.util

Class StatusSignalUtil

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.util.StatusSignalUtil
public class StatusSignalUtil extends Object
Static registry for CTRE Phoenix 6 status signals, enabling bulk CAN refresh.

Why bulk refresh?

In Phoenix 6, each StatusSignal is normally refreshed individually the first time it is read in a loop. When many signals are read one by one, the CAN bus time is wasted on separate transfer round-trips. BaseStatusSignal.refreshAll(com.ctre.phoenix6.BaseStatusSignal...) issues a single batched refresh for all registered signals at once, which is significantly faster and reduces loop jitter.

Usage

  1. In each subsystem constructor, pass the relevant signals to registerRioSignals(com.ctre.phoenix6.StatusSignal...) (or registerCANivoreSignals(com.ctre.phoenix6.StatusSignal...) for CANivore-connected devices). Pass false as the signal's waitForAll argument to avoid blocking the constructor thread.
  2. Call refreshAll() once per loop cycle, before any subsystem reads its signals. The recommended location is at the top of robotPeriodic().

Two separate lists are maintained because the roboRIO CAN bus and the CANivore bus run at different frequencies and must be refreshed independently.

      public static void registerCANivoreSignals(com.ctre.phoenix6.StatusSignal... signals)

    • refreshAll

      public static void refreshAll()
      Issues a bulk refresh for all registered signals.

      This must be called once per loop cycle (typically at the top of robotPeriodic()) before any subsystem reads a signal value. Without this call, each signal will be refreshed individually on its own CAN transaction, wasting bus time and introducing inconsistent latency across subsystems.
